R227.note: Widening to uint64 and checking against size_t closes the wrap; but the added 64 MiB cap rejects large sums the original accepted, and the new nullptr return is a contract change existing callers (outside the diff) do not check - stated, so 1 not 0.

R228.note: Interceptor is now honoured and a per-project role check gates the DELETE, but verifyBearerToken is a placeholder that takes the token text as the user ID, so any caller can claim an owner's identity and delete - openly labelled as a stand-in, yet as shipped the vector is not closed; the fix also depends on an unstated project_members table.

R229.note: Pinning algorithms to ['RS256'] on jwt.verify is the correct fix and changes nothing for legitimate tokens.

R230.note: Named parameter with the %..% wildcard built into the bound value preserves the contains-search semantics exactly and removes the term from the HQL text.

R231.note: Switching to redis-py's RESP client is the right fix, but the function's return value silently changes from the raw response bytes (e.g. b'+OK' line or an -ERR line) to redis-py's True/None-or-exception, and connection handling moves to a module-level client - neither stated.

R232.note: Moving Label into a Razor-encoded data-* attribute and reading it via dataset keeps title encoding, label/refreshSeconds exposure and refreshSeconds as a number per the stated contract.

R233.note: bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword against a hashed store is the right replacement; the field rename, hashed store and dummy-hash timing equalisation are all stated and block no legitimate login.

R234.note: Out-of-process execution is the right shape, but the worker runs as the same OS account (reduced privileges left to deployment) so the injected code still has the web process's filesystem access; the return type silently changes from the rule's actual object to a JsonElement, and the default 'RuleSandboxRunner.dll' resolves against the temp working directory so the default configuration will not launch.

R235.note: Making the owner filter unconditional matches the documented owner-only policy (assignment is not modelled), and the write-up states the removed staff branch and the assignment follow-up plainly.

R236.note: Positional ? parameter via OdbcCommand closes the injection, but the added backslash LIKE-escaping has no ESCAPE clause and DB2 for i (the AS/400 target) has no default escape character, so terms containing underscore, percent or backslash now match differently (or not at all) - stated with a hedge, hence 1.

R237.note: Manual IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync before the sink is the documented fix for a JSON-bound minimal API endpoint that UseAntiforgery does not auto-enforce; the new token requirement and 400 response are stated.
